title: Ripples in 2D Materials Revealed by Multislice Electron Ptychography with Adaptive Free Path
content: The shape of nanostructures and the ripples in two-dimensional (2D) materials are pivotal to their chemical properties [1, 2]. However, traditional imaging techniques are often limited to two-dimensional projections, making it difficult to obtain comprehensive 3D structural information. Electron ptychography, as a computational imaging method, uses two-dimensional diffraction patterns at each scanning point in a two-dimensional sample plane (i.e., 4D data) [3, 4]. Through algorithmic iterations, it can decouple the illumination beam and object phase information [5-7], thereby achieving high-precision, high-resolution, aberration-free imaging results. This technique has recently gained significant attention [8-14].
